title: Proton’s Lumo, a privacy-focused alternative to ChatGPT and Claude, arrives on desktop
lede: Proton has released Lumo Desktop for Windows, macOS and Linux, letting its assistant act on local files, folders and connected apps under permission rules the user sets per connector.

points: Connectors include file-system access, shell execution, browser fetching, Proton's email app, Confluence, Dropbox and Jira.
Local and remote MCP servers can be added as connectors.
For each connector, users mark actions as automatic, needing approval, or blocked; scheduled tasks carry their own permission sets.
Proton says chat history is encrypted so only the user can read it, with no server-side logs and data hosted in Europe under Swiss law.
Skills store reusable instructions, templates and reference files, replacing the earlier Custom Lumos.

sections.text: Allow, approve and block levels per connector are a concrete pattern for scoping what a desktop agent may touch, a question every team shipping local agents now has to answer.
